def: The paper, repository, weights and benchmark numbers that together support a research claim, built for other researchers rather than for users.
Re-running a published method and obtaining a result consistent with the paper, kept distinct from testing whether it transfers to new data.
Whether a method that works on a paper's benchmark still works on a different distribution such as a customer's own documents.
The written promise of what a service accepts, what it returns, how it fails and what will not change without notice.
A deterministic check run on a model's output before it is returned, such as confirming that every number in a summary appears in the source.
A cheaper, weaker answer returned, and clearly labelled, when the main path times out or fails.
A service-level indicator: a measurement of behaviour, such as the fraction of requests answered within 2.5 seconds.
A service-level objective: a target for an indicator over a period, such as 99% within 2.5 seconds over 30 days.
The shortfall an objective allows, such as 1% of requests being slow, which when spent shifts priority from features to reliability.
A short document stating a model's intended use, evaluation data, performance by slice and known limitations.
A customer-facing statement of what a system was tested on, where it is weakest and what it must not be relied on for.
